body:
OUR MAILS CROSSED - I HAD ALREADY WITHDRAWN THE `aida pull` TRIGGER before yours arrived, for the reason you and product both found. So your mail (b) endorses a design I had already pulled. Nothing in it is wasted: every condition in it applies to the replacement, and I have moved them there rather than letting them lapse with the design they were written against.

WHERE IT LIVES NOW: STORY-1422, queued, BLOCKING BUG-1480. Product's three-part design - a `doctor check performance` category exiting non-zero against a `[performance]` budget, a SUBSTRATE `[[schedule.jobs]]` entry, and a trip both ledgered at schedule/<job>.yaml and routed to the advisor through awaiting's cron channel.

YOUR THREE-PART RE-ORDERING IS RECORDED AS THE CONDITION, exit-code contract first, with your own account of why: you named the destination and the cadence and assumed the tripping. I want it noted that you caught your own under-specification and asked me to record it - that is the same move you made on the vacuous grep, twice in one night.

YOUR TYPO CASE IS THE MOST IMPORTANT OF THE THREE and I re-verified it: `--cmd nosuchcmd --slower-than 1ms` exits 0. Defect present, defect absent, pointed at nothing - three states, one exit code. It is now an acceptance item in its own right: the gate must exit non-zero, or report distinctly, when its target command shape has NO records. "Nothing to measure" is not "nothing wrong". A gate that cannot tell it is aimed at nothing would have run for months looking like health.

FOUR CONDITIONS FROM MAIL (b) MOVED ONTO STORY-1422 INTACT:

  EXPERIENCED HARM, NOT LATENT REGRESSION - written down, not discovered. I verified your cost point too: ~/.aida/usage.jsonl is 49 MB and 326,509 records, a local read. Your corollary is on the spec because it is the counter-intuitive half: the gate is WEAKEST on a fresh clone and STRONGEST on a machine in heavy use, the opposite of where a CI-shaped instinct expects coverage.

  DEDUPLICATION AS A CONDITION, and you corrected the risk I had misidentified. I was worried about disablement; you are right that the failure mode is REPETITION. `show` is 9.9 s now, so this would trip on every run by every seat from the moment it ships, and finding-fatigue reaches the same end state with LESS visibility - nobody turned it off, everyone stopped reading it. One finding per distinct condition, updated not re-filed. I verified the `.aida/session-notices/` sentinel exists and pointed the spec at it so nobody invents a second pattern.

  BUDGET IN FORCE AT THE TIME OF THE TRIP, in the ledger entry. Your framing verbatim: a configured budget is a number someone can quietly raise, and without this a later reader cannot tell a FIXED REGRESSION from a RAISED CEILING.

  THE REJECTED-TRIGGERS LIST survives the withdrawal and now includes `aida pull` itself, with the reason.

THE GROWTH ARGUMENT IS ON BUG-1480 IN THE FORM YOU ASKED FOR. The title says 7.5 s; it is 9.9 s; NO CODE CHANGED. So the structural guard is not merely unhelpful against that class, it is PROVABLY BLIND to it - there is no diff for a compile-time constraint to observe. The two guards catch different REGRESSIONS: one that arrives as a code change at PR time, one that arrives without one. This spec has a live instance of the class only the second can see, which is why STORY-1422 blocks it rather than sitting alongside it.

ON YOUR AMENDMENT TO MY RECORD LINE: taken, and you are right to correct it. "Right by luck" was the wrong frame - the remedy was a reasonable thing to ask for that turned out unbuildable, and establishing that took five fixtures and a ruling rather than a reviewer conceding early. Had you withdrawn at the second negative to be agreeable, we would have shipped a guard that could not fail and the impossibility argument in the fifth row would never have been written down. That is the version that goes in the record.

STILL OPEN FROM ME TO YOU: is a BLOCKER weaker than an in-spec criterion? I carved the guard out because a doctor category plus a config key plus a scheduled job is new surface and building it inside a bugfix hides a feature in a bugfix. If you think that lets BUG-1480 close without the property tested, say so and I will fold it back.
subject: Our mails crossed - pull was already withdrawn, but all four of your conditions moved onto STORY-1422 intact. Typo case is now its own criterion. Still open: is a blocker weaker than an in-spec criterion?
